description: Chaotic oscillator that moves a particle along the Rucklidge attractor and puts out its three coordinates as smooth, unpredictable voltages, anywhere from very slow modulation to audio rate

params.text: Sets how fast the simulation runs, from -7 to +7, each unit doubling the rate; right-clicking adds turbo mode, which multiplies the rate by a further 32
Sets the A constant of the attractor from 3.8 to 6.7, a simple repeating loop counter-clockwise and a strongly chaotic orbit clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the speed CV; at a wide enough setting the CV covers the whole knob range
Attenuates and inverts the chaos CV; at a wide enough setting the CV covers the whole knob range
Adds a Tricorder to the right, which plots the particle's path in 3D
Adds a Chaops to the left, which adds memory, morph, cruise and freeze controls

inputs.text: Varies the rate the simulation runs at
Varies the A constant of the attractor

outputs.text: The x coordinate of the particle; right-clicking this port inverts its voltage, which is reflected in the P output and in anything graphing to the right
The y coordinate of the particle; right-clicking this port inverts its voltage, which is reflected in the P output and in anything graphing to the right
The z coordinate of the particle; right-clicking this port inverts its voltage, which is reflected in the P output and in anything graphing to the right
The particle's position as a 3-channel polyphonic signal, x on channel 1, y on channel 2 and z on channel 3

menu: Turbo mode: +5 speed — adds 5 to the speed setting, a factor of 32; it is on the panel menu and on the SPEED knob's own menu
Flash panel when overflow reset occurs — turns off the panel flash that marks a reset after the simulation overflows
Insert Tricorder on right — adds a Tricorder to the right, which plots the particle's path in 3D
Insert Chaops on left — adds a Chaops to the left, which adds memory, morph, cruise and freeze controls
Configure for V/OCT — on the SPEED attenuverter's own menu, not the panel menu: sets that attenuverter so the speed CV tracks a volt per octave
Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero
Flip voltage polarity — on the X, Y or Z output port's own menu, not the panel menu: inverts that port's voltage, which is reflected in the P output and in anything graphing to the right
